concerns.text: The three Edge Cases specify required behaviors (sample rows or drop high-cardinality columns when RAM limit is exceeded; log non-convergence, record NaN metrics, and continue; flag zero-variance synthetic columns without crashing the KS-test) but no FR covers any of them. FR-001..FR-008 do not mention memory-overflow mitigation, failure handling for non-converging generators, or zero-variance column handling. Add FRs (e.g., FR-009..FR-011) anchored to US-1/US-2 so these behaviors are buildable and testable.

US-2 scenario 3 requires 'a summary table showing the mean and standard deviation of metric differences across all evaluated datasets and methods', but no FR explicitly covers the aggregation/summary-table step. FR-004/FR-005 compute per-dataset metrics; FR-008 covers the final report. Add an aggregation clause to FR-004/FR-005 or a new FR anchored to US-2.

Edge case 1 references 'a specific dataset (e.g., Higgs)' but FR-001 and the Assumptions section enumerate only UCI Adult, Credit Card Fraud, Covertype. Higgs appears nowhere else in the spec — either add it to the dataset list or use one of the named datasets in the edge case to avoid an implicit scope shift.

FR-007 says the sensitivity sweep reports 'variation in false-positive/false-negative rates', while US-3 scenario 2 says it re-evaluates 'headline inconsistency rates' and how 'faithful vs. unfaithful' classification changes. These are three different terms for the same output; pick one stable term so the reported quantity is unambiguous.

SC-003 measures correlation distortion 'against the baseline of random noise', but no FR or user story requires generating a random-noise baseline. The cross-reference (FR-004) does not cover this; either add the baseline to an FR or drop it from SC-003.

US-1 scenario 3 requires training to terminate 'earlier if early stopping criteria are met', but FR-002 mandates 'default hyperparameters' with only a 30-epoch cap and never mentions early stopping. State whether early stopping is in scope so the two requirements cannot be read as conflicting.

FR-007 requires reporting 'false-positive/false-negative rates' across the threshold sweep, but no ground truth is defined for which columns/pairs are truly faithful. Without a labeled truth set (or a defined proxy, e.g., synthetic-vs-real-holdout as null and a deliberately corrupted dataset as positive control), FP/FN are not computable. Specify the reference against which errors are counted.

'measured against the baseline of random noise' — the random-noise baseline is not operationally defined (row/column count, distribution family, seed). Specify how the noise baseline is generated so the comparison is reproducible.

'Stability of the faithful/unfaithful classification' lacks a measure. State what is reported, e.g., the fraction of column/method classifications that change across thresholds {0.01, 0.05, 0.1}, so the criterion is checkable.

Edge case cites Higgs exceeding 7GB during one-hot encoding, but FR-001's dataset list is Adult/Fraud/Covertype and Higgs appears nowhere in requirements. Either name the reachable high-cardinality trigger within the selected datasets or drop Higgs; as written the demanded edge case may not be reachable under the supported domain.

Under-reach: the idea's methodology explicitly requires 'Statistical summarization: perform paired t-tests or Wilcoxon signed-rank tests on the collection of metric differences to assess overall superiority of any method.' No FR or SC covers this cross-method comparison; the spec only aggregates means/SDs (US-2 scenario 3). Add an FR for paired significance testing of per-method metric differences.

Under-reach: the idea requires 'marginal PDFs (via kernel density estimates)' and visualization artifacts ('side-by-side histograms, QQ-plots, and correlation heatmaps'). The spec computes KS/Chi-square statistics but drops KDE-based marginal comparison and all visualization outputs. Either add these or explicitly scope them out in Assumptions.

Under-reach (minor): the idea's preprocessing includes 'standardize numerics, and split into train/hold-out sets.' FR-001 covers imputation and encoding only; the train/hold-out split is absent. If the hold-out is intentionally dropped (synthetic data compared against training set), state this as an explicit assumption; otherwise add it.

Under-reach (minor): the idea specifies DP-GAN as 'privacy-budget-controlled'; FR-002 trains all three models with 'default hyperparameters' with no privacy-budget (epsilon) setting or recording. Clarify whether the DP budget is configured and reported, since it affects interpretability of DP-GAN's divergence.

Fidelity is evaluated by comparing synthetic data against the SAME real dataset used to train the generators (FR-003 generates row counts 'matching the real training set'; FR-004/SC-002 compare real vs synthetic marginals). The idea's methodology sketch included a train/hold-out split, but the spec dropped it. This is a partial circularity: a generator that overfits/memorizes training data scores perfectly on this comparison, so 'high fidelity' cannot be distinguished from memorization. The spec must compare synthetic data against a held-out real split (or explicitly acknowledge and bound this confound).

Fisher's z-test for correlation differences assumes two INDEPENDENT samples. The synthetic sample is generated from a model fit on the real data, so real and synthetic correlations are dependent; the nominal p-values and the p<0.05 flagging in US-2 scenario 2 will be miscalibrated. A permutation/bootstrap-based comparison of correlation matrices would be valid here; Fisher's z as specified is not.

Classifying columns as 'faithful' when p ≥ 0.05 (after correction) is accepting the null. With synthetic row counts equal to the full training set (tens of thousands of rows for Adult/Covertype), KS/chi-square tests have power to detect trivially small deviations, so 'unfaithful' flags will be driven by N, not by practical fidelity. The spec mentions effect sizes in FR-005 but SC-002's faithful/unfaithful dichotomy (and the sensitivity sweep in FR-007/SC-004) is defined purely on p-value thresholds. Classification should incorporate effect-size criteria (e.g., KS statistic magnitude), not significance alone.

Single training run per (model, dataset) combination with no seed replication. GAN training is high-variance; a single 30-epoch run per cell gives no estimate of run-to-run variability, so 'method A distorts correlations more than method B' claims (the core research question) rest on n=1 per cell. The idea sketch's paired t-tests/Wilcoxon across metric differences implicitly require replicates. The spec should require multiple seeds (or at minimum justify single-run conclusions as illustrative).

SC-003's 'baseline of random noise' comparator is underspecified: random noise on categorical columns or on standardized marginals is not defined, and a generator that only matches marginals (e.g., CopulaGAN by construction) will trivially beat a marginal-destroying noise baseline on correlation metrics. Specify the null generator (e.g., independent columns with matched marginals) — which is also the more informative baseline.

new_concerns.text: FR-007 states the sensitivity analysis uses the **control‑perturbation dataset defined in FR‑022**, but the dataset is actually defined in FR‑021. This cross‑reference is incorrect and may cause confusion; update the reference to FR‑021.

Over‑reach: FR‑019 introduces a random‑noise baseline dataset and FR‑021/FR‑022 define a control‑perturbation dataset for sensitivity analysis. These artifacts and the associated SC‑003 were not part of the original idea, which only required marginal and correlation fidelity metrics and a basic threshold sensitivity analysis. Adding these analyses expands the scope beyond what was requested.

Constitution principle VI still requires reporting Fisher’s z‑transformed correlation deviations, yet FR‑005 and the implementation now specify a permutation‑based correlation test. This creates a contradictory requirement between the governing constitution and the functional specification, risking non‑reproducible methodology.
